# Policy-proposal + world-model-scoring system (auto-generated by analysis/decision_system.py)

## 1. `C_decision ≈ I·K·H·U·C_transition` instantiated with V-JEPA 2-AC

- Settings from `vjepa2/notebooks/utils/world_model_wrapper.py`: I=10, K=400, H=2, U=1 → 8,000 transitions per decision.
- Predictor FLOPs per decision: 1,962 TFLOP → **245 GFLOP per transition** (h=1: 159, h=2: 331; frame-causal predictor re-processes earlier frames).
- GPT/05's illustrative value is 40 MFLOP per transition (compact latent). A token-based latent (256 tokens × 1024-d per frame) costs **~6,000× more** per transition.
- Candidate state slice (K=400, S=258, D=1024, BF16): 202 MiB — GPT/05's 128-token row (64 MiB) is the right order of magnitude for this class.

| K | pi0 ms (Thor) | expert AI | scorer ms (Thor) | total Thor ms | total H100 ms |

| 2 | 42.6 | 116 | 12.8 | 55.4 | 8.1 |
| 4 | 43.9 | 219 | 15.5 | 59.5 | 9.2 |
| 8 | 46.7 | 396 | 23.0 | 69.7 | 12.2 |
| 16 | 52.2 | 663 | 38.1 | 90.3 | 19.2 |
| 32 | 65.7 | 1,001 | 68.4 | 134.1 | 33.4 |
| 64 | 113.0 | 1,342 | 129.0 | 242.0 | 61.6 |

Because the action expert is weight-bandwidth-bound at K=1 (AI ≈ 60), sampling 16 candidate chunks costs only ~25% more policy time on Thor: the extra candidates ride on weight reads that were happening anyway. The scorer then dominates beyond K≈16.
